title: Switch dictation to Vulkan when a GPU is present
head: 9e6f383a3cf8
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Skip GPU switching on aarch64, where voxtype-bin supplies no Vulkan binary
leads.consequence: On an Apple Silicon machine with vulkan-asahi's ICD installed, omarchy-hw-vulkan returns success. The aarch64 voxtype-bin package contains only voxtype-cpu and voxtype-onnx, so upstream gpu::enable() returns an error before switching. With set -e, the installer exits after installing the package and downloading the model, without running setup systemd, reload, shell restart, or the ready notification. The install menu then disables retry on package presence; the already-emitted first-run invitation is not re-sent. A manual retry repeats the failure. Add an architecture/backend-availability check before the sudo call, or treat an unavailable GPU variant as a CPU-only install with a clear warning.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F2; first-run invitation one-shot detail verified by coordinator (install-voxtype.hook:5); published as aarch64 finding

leads.summary: Existing Voxtype installations do not get the GPU switch on upgrade
leads.consequence: The new sudo step only runs in the interactive installer. On an existing installation originally left on the CPU binary, an Omarchy upgrade does not invoke that installer; the Voxtype package's pre_upgrade/post_upgrade saves and restores the selected binary. The package-presence guard disables the menu install entry and the invitation is once-only. Existing users stay on CPU indefinitely until they explicitly rerun a command; if a service is already running, merely switching the link without restarting it also leaves that daemon on CPU until restart. Open PR #7129 provides a migration for the avx2/avx512 CPU-link case and merges cleanly with this change; consider incorporating or coordinating a migration (including other CPU variants where applicable) and a user-service restart.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus existing-installs note; #7129 migration mentioned in Related open PRs; not a separate finding (product decision)

leads.summary: ICD-file presence is not a check that Vulkan transcription can run
leads.consequence: The guard checks for any .json in /usr/share/vulkan/icd.d, not whether an actual compatible device or successful inference exists. Upstream gpu::enable checks binary existence, warns rather than errors when even libvulkan is missing, and its variant probe only executes --version before pointing /usr/bin/voxtype to the Vulkan binary. Therefore an ICD for an incompatible GPU (such as the Haswell exception targeted in #11481) can select a nonworking backend and still reach the ready notification; without the Vulkan binary (as in H1) the newly fatal switch instead aborts an otherwise viable CPU install. Use device/backend verification with a CPU fallback or isolate GPU failure handling; actual transcription failure on specific devices remains hardware-dependent and was not run here.
leads.triage: covered by Opus F1 and Opus's evidence that no-usable-device machines fall back to CPU inside the Vulkan build; no separate finding

leads.summary: A manual reinstall can change a preselected ONNX backend and erase local configuration
leads.consequence: When someone reruns the installer with voxtype-bin already installed, omarchy-pkg-add --needed does not reset the chosen /usr/bin/voxtype link. cp overwrites the existing user's config, then the newly privileged gpu --enable consults the active binary to choose Whisper Vulkan or ONNX CUDA/MIGraphX, irrespective of the overwritten configuration. On a machine with an ONNX CPU selection, the call can either replace the user's backend with a GPU-specific ONNX binary or fail before installing the user service if no GPU backend is available. Preserve existing config and binary choices, and scope automatic switching to a genuinely fresh install (or explicitly ask to change backend). The config overwrite predates this PR, but the now-effective privileged backend change and failure are introduced by it.
leads.triage: behavioural; neutral follow-up to Opus (opus/followup-1.md) confirmed from source; published in collapsed More findings, marked not reproduced

leads.summary: Resolve the conflicting Haswell GPU guard in open PR #11481
leads.consequence: PR #11481 adds omarchy-hw-intel-haswell-gpu before the broad Vulkan check, intentionally keeps Haswell on CPU, and calls sudo gpu --disable on reinstall. This PR's new hunk changes the exact same conditional; a three-way merge against #11481's own base yields conflict markers at lines 18-31. Taking this PR's side without retaining the new guard reinstates GPU selection on Haswell. Resolve by keeping the hardware exception and this PR's privileged GPU call on the non-Haswell branch, then ensure the tests for both branches survive. #11481's description says hasvk crashes in model loading, but this hunt did not independently reproduce that driver-level failure.

leads.summary: Resolve alternative GPU failure and NPU/fresh-only branches in open Voxtype PRs
leads.consequence: Open PR #12901 also introduces sudo but explicitly warns and continues with CPU when GPU selection fails, whereas this PR aborts. #5177 skips the GPU step after selecting an Intel NPU ONNX build; lifting this PR's unconditional Vulkan branch outside that else would run GPU enable on the wrong engine. #13098 restricts GPU selection to fresh installs while preserving existing config; keeping an unconditional sudo call would undo that protection. Three-way merges with each PR's own base produce conflict markers around the changed lines, so Git does not choose the right policy automatically. Decide the intended failure policy explicitly, keep the NPU branch exclusive and preserve #13098's fresh-only guard if those PRs merge.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F3 (#12901, #5177, #13098 conflicts); #12901 mentioned in Related open PRs

leads.summary: The new success test accepts a sudo call that makes no backend change
leads.consequence: The sudo stub logs its arguments and executes the same unprivileged voxtype stub; voxtype itself just logs and returns 0. There is no simulated root permission check, /usr/bin/voxtype link, or assertion that the Vulkan backend was actually selected. A plausible regression where sudo succeeds but the GPU subcommand returns success without changing the active binary passes the claimed success test. Require a temporary active-binary symlink and model a privileged switch in the stubs, then assert its target, or run Voxtype's real switching logic only within an isolated fixture. Retain the failure-path assertion too.
leads.triage: close to Opus test nits; not published as such (no demonstrated benefit beyond Opus's case-3 anchoring note, which is published as Optional test improvement)

leads.summary: Coordinate the colliding installer test pathname with open PRs #7890 and #8316
leads.consequence: Both open PRs add a different test/shell.d/voxtype-install-test.sh from the same empty base path; #7890 exercises CPUs lacking AVX2 and #8316 tests a source-build fallback. When either lands, Git cannot keep both additions at that filename automatically; replacing one suite with this PR's new test silently drops its CPU coverage. #8316 also rewrites the entire installer and GitHub marks it CONFLICTING against current quattro, even before this PR. Keep the CPU tests by merging assertions into a single test file or using separate named tests, and reconcile the install script together.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F3; published in Related open PRs

## What worked
- The Sol hunt and Opus converged independently on aarch64, Haswell/#11481 and the #7129 overlap. The hunt's one new behavioural lead (a re-run over an existing backend) was settled by a single neutral follow-up.
- The Opus self-check caught four real errors that had crept in while compressing the text to 1,500 characters: a lost "no other GPU" qualifier, "no service exists", overstated impact on existing installs, and ordering in the sequence.

## Friction
- A network outage after the host woke from sleep interrupted both reviewers.
  - Sol's run 1 exited 0 even though its last turn had stopReason=error. `pi_job.py wait/status` reports exit 0 as a normal exit, so completion looked clean. Suggestion: have `pi_job.py` surface the final stopReason, and flag a missing `hunt.json`.
- The first self-check SendMessage was queued while the agent was finishing its follow-up turn. The coordinator resent it, and the agent did the check once.
- The editorial check caught placement issues in two rounds:
  - a collapsed note that read as a finding;
  - a Haswell sequence that sat after the wrong finding.

  Drafting lesson: every behaviour-change note goes in a More findings block with all its parts, and each Details block goes directly after the finding it supports.
- The coordinator's first `cat team-1.json` exceeded the tool output limit (the team history is large). Read registry fields with `jq` instead.

## Carry forward
- For small installer PRs, the 1,500-character visible budget is tight with two findings. Budget roughly 700 characters for the fixed header and footer.
comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** With `sudo`, the switch now affects Haswell iGPUs and aarch64, where Vulkan dictation fails.

### Haswell iGPUs get a crashing Vulkan build

`omarchy-hw-vulkan` accepts any ICD file, and `vulkan-intel` installs one for every Intel GPU. On a Haswell iGPU with no other supported GPU, the Vulkan build aborts at model load, restarting every 5 s, while the installer still reports ready (#11370). **Impact:** new installs there crash-loop instead of staying on CPU. Not reproduced.

**Suggested change:** Keep Haswell on the CPU build, as #11481 does.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Haswell sequence (source-traced, Voxtype 1.1.0, whisper-rs-sys 0.15.0, Mesa 26.2.3):**

```text
install/hardware/vulkan.sh      -> vulkan-intel on any Intel GPU (ships intel_hasvk_icd.json)
omarchy-hw-vulkan               -> true (any *.json in icd.d)
sudo voxtype setup gpu --enable -> succeeds (only checks voxtype-vulkan --version)
voxtype.service model load      -> ggml_vk_get_device: "Unsupported device" (no 16-bit storage)
                                -> uncaught C++ exception across FFI, abort
Restart=on-failure, RestartSec=5 -> crash loop; installer still says "Voxtype Dictation Ready"
```
</details>

### aarch64 installs stop halfway

aarch64 `voxtype-bin` ships no `voxtype-vulkan`, so with any Vulkan ICD the switch fails and `set -e` exits before `voxtype setup systemd`. **Impact:** Install > Dictation shows as installed, but the service is never set up.

**Suggested change:** Also require `[[ -x /usr/lib/voxtype/voxtype-vulkan ]]`.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 9e6f383)</summary>

# Reproducer: aarch64 install stops after the Vulkan switch fails

Stub-based test in the style of `test/shell.d/voxtype-install-test.sh`. Save it as `test/shell.d/voxtype-install-arch-test.sh` and run `bash test/shell.d/voxtype-install-arch-test.sh`. It stubs every command the installer calls (nothing touches the host) and models the two `voxtype-bin` 1.1.0 package layouts: x86_64 ships `/usr/lib/voxtype/voxtype-vulkan`; aarch64 ships the `voxtype-cpu` and `voxtype-onnx` engine binaries and no `voxtype-vulkan`. The `voxtype` stub mirrors `enable()` in Voxtype 1.1.0 `src/setup/gpu.rs`, which returns "Vulkan backend not installed" when that binary is missing.

It is a model of the package, not a run on aarch64 hardware.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

test_home=$(mktemp -d)
test_bin=$(mktemp -d)
omarchy_path=$(mktemp -d)
voxtype_lib=$(mktemp -d)
log_file=$(mktemp)

cleanup() {
  rm -rf "$test_home" "$test_bin" "$omarchy_path" "$voxtype_lib"
  rm -f "$log_file"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

mkdir -p "$omarchy_path/default/voxtype"
printf 'engine = "whisper"\n' >"$omarchy_path/default/voxtype/config.toml"

write_stub() {
  local name="$1"
  local body="$2"
  printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/bash' "$body" >"$test_bin/$name"
  chmod +x "$test_bin/$name"
}

write_stub gum '[[ $1 == confirm ]] && exit 0
exit 1'
write_stub omarchy-pkg-add 'exit 0'
write_stub hyprctl 'echo "hyprctl:$*" >>"$TEST_LOG"'
write_stub omarchy-restart-shell 'exit 0'
write_stub omarchy-notification-send 'echo "notify:$*" >>"$TEST_LOG"'
write_stub systemctl 'echo "systemctl:$*" >>"$TEST_LOG"'
# omarchy-hw-vulkan only looks for an ICD JSON, which Mesa's vulkan-* packages
# install on aarch64 too.
write_stub omarchy-hw-vulkan 'exit 0'
write_stub sudo 'echo "sudo:$*" >>"$TEST_LOG"
"$@"'
# Mirrors voxtype 1.1.0 src/setup/gpu.rs enable(): on the Whisper engine it
# bails before touching /usr/bin/voxtype when no voxtype-vulkan binary exists.
write_stub voxtype 'echo "voxtype:$*" >>"$TEST_LOG"
if [[ $* == "setup gpu --enable" && ! -e $VOXTYPE_LIB/voxtype-vulkan ]]; then
  printf "Error: Vulkan backend not installed.\nThe voxtype-vulkan binary was not found in /usr/lib/voxtype\n" >&2
  exit 1
fi
exit 0'

run_install() {
  : >"$log_file"
  local status=0
  HOME="$test_home" \
    OMARCHY_PATH="$omarchy_path" \
    PATH="$test_bin:$PATH" \
    TEST_LOG="$log_file" \
    VOXTYPE_LIB="$voxtype_lib" \
    bash "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-voxtype-install" || status=$?
  echo "--- installer exit $status, calls:"
  cat "$log_file"
  return "$status"
}

# x86_64 voxtype-bin ships a Vulkan build next to the CPU builds.
touch "$voxtype_lib/voxtype-avx2" "$voxtype_lib/voxtype-avx512" "$voxtype_lib/voxtype-vulkan"
run_install || fail "an x86_64 install with a Vulkan driver finishes"
grep -qx 'voxtype:setup systemd' "$log_file" || fail "an x86_64 install sets up the dictation service"
grep -q '^notify:.*Voxtype Dictation Ready' "$log_file" || fail "an x86_64 install reports dictation ready"
pass "an x86_64 install with a Vulkan driver finishes"

# aarch64 voxtype-bin 1.1.0 ships only voxtype-cpu and voxtype-onnx.
rm -f "$voxtype_lib"/*
touch "$voxtype_lib/voxtype-cpu" "$voxtype_lib/voxtype-onnx"
run_install || fail "an aarch64 install with a Vulkan driver finishes on the CPU build"
grep -qx 'voxtype:setup systemd' "$log_file" || fail "an aarch64 install sets up the dictation service"
grep -q '^notify:.*Voxtype Dictation Ready' "$log_file" || fail "an aarch64 install reports dictation ready"
pass "an aarch64 install with a Vulkan driver finishes on the CPU build"
```

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Related open PRs:** #7129 makes the same one-line change and adds a migration for existing installs (it merges cleanly with this PR). #12901 makes the same change but warns and continues on the CPU build when the switch fails. #11481 conflicts on the same block. #7890 and #8316 each add a different `test/shell.d/voxtype-install-test.sh`.

**Verified:**
- `voxtype setup gpu --enable` rewrites the root-owned `/usr/bin/voxtype`, so it needs root; under `sudo` (default environment) it writes nothing in the user's home.
- On x86_64 with a working Vulkan GPU, `voxtype setup systemd` runs afterwards, so the daemon starts on the Vulkan build, and package upgrades keep the choice.
- The new test fails at the merge-base (no `sudo` line; the failed switch exits 0) and passes at this head.

**Optional test improvement:** the failure case only checks for a non-zero exit, so any unrelated failure passes it. Asserting the `sudo:voxtype setup gpu --enable` line and the absence of `voxtype:setup systemd` would tie it to the switch.
</details>

<details><summary>More findings</summary>

### Re-running the installer overrides a chosen backend

`setup gpu --enable` follows the active `/usr/bin/voxtype`, not the config, so a re-run with `omarchy voxtype install` re-enables Vulkan after a manual `sudo voxtype setup gpu --disable` (the Haswell workaround in #11370). On an ONNX backend it switches to an ONNX GPU build, or on CPUs without AVX-512 fails with "No compatible ONNX GPU backend found" and stops before `voxtype setup systemd`. **Impact:** a deliberate backend choice is undone, or the re-run ends as a failed install; the merge-base left the backend unchanged. Source-traced, not reproduced.

**Suggested change:** Switch only when `readlink -f /usr/bin/voxtype` is a `voxtype-avx*` CPU build, as the #7129 migration does.
</details>
